page: Amazon Web Services c1.medium is a first-generation compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor and utilizing an i386 CPU architecture. The server is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor operating at 1.8 GHz, delivering two dedicated physical cores across two vCPUs without hyperthreading. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 0.85 GB of RAM per core, along with 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a shared 30 MB L3 cache. Hardware acceleration features are minimal, lacking AVX and modern instruction sets, though AES cryptography is present. Local non-volatile capacity is provisioned via a 350 GB HDD drive, while network bandwidth baseline is rated at 0 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark measurements indicate legacy-tier performance across compute, memory, and application operations. Synthetic testing records a stress-ng single-core score of 1196.18 and a multi-core score of 1605.88, both falling in the lower percentiles. Geekbench evaluation yields a single-core score of 493.0 and a multi-core score of 677.0, with PassMark CPU overall scoring 1433.17. The memory subsystem delivers 11.86 GB/s read and 10.27 GB/s write throughput on large 256 MB blocks, matching PassMark memory scores of 804.82. Application workloads show 0.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.54 GB/s of static web serving throughput.

Due to its aging CPU generation, restricted 32-bit architectural ecosystem, and low memory ceiling, the instance exhibits poor compute density and throughput compared to modern virtualized alternatives. The presence of 350 GB HDD storage provides basic scratch space, but spinning disks limit random input and output speeds. The instance is primarily relevant for legacy 32-bit workloads, simple utilities, or non-critical background processing where low baseline CPU allocation suffices.
description: Amazon Web Services c1.medium is a legacy compute-optimized instance powered by a dual-core Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor clocked at 1.8 GHz on an i386 architecture. The instance provisions two dedicated vCPUs with one thread per core, backed by 2.0 GB of system memory and 350 GB of bundled local HDD storage. Operating on the Xen hypervisor, it includes AES instruction support but lacks modern vector extensions such as AVX. Empirical benchmark evaluations reflect entry-level performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 1433.17, Geekbench single-core and multi-core ratings of 493.0 and 677.0, and 10.27 GB/s large-block memory write throughput. The baseline network allocation is rated at 0 Gbps. Given its restrained compute capacity, spinning disk storage, and modest RAM allocation, c1.medium is suitable only for legacy 32-bit environments, basic test routines, and low-priority batch utilities.
